quest.title: The Coming of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: The Sabzeruz Festival is about to begin. As agreed, you return to Sumeru City to find Dunyarzad and take part in the festival together.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Mora x31175, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There she is! Dunyarzad, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Just as promised, Traveler and Paimon! I'm so glad that you two came back to celebrate Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday.

choices.text: Looks like we made it back in time.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe, indeed! The festival is tomorrow. We have been preparing for so long that I can't help but feel a little nervous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no need to be nervous! Paimon's sure that Lesser Lord Kusanali will feel everyone's gratitude.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe, thanks, Paimon. I hope that everyone who comes to the festival will also have a good time.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Speaking of which, did you manage to make your way to Port Ormos? Discover anything over there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course we went! A lot of things happened there...

choices.text: Unfortunately, we didn't find any new information on Lesser Lord Kusanali.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: *sigh* I see. Sounds like you two had another exciting adventure...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...If there is another chance, I would love to join...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: *sigh* My lady, if you went to Port Ormos in your current state, we'd both be in for a lifetime of trouble.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dehya! You were eavesdropping!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Ahem, it's called covert protection! Keeping an ear out for what's going on around my employer is part of the job.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It's alright, Dehya. I merely said that I "would" like to go. I know better than to think my body could handle it, hehe.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: The festival is tomorrow. I've been doing nothing but causing trouble for you, so Dehya, please take some time to relax. I'll be fine.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Hm, even when you put it that way, it still doesn't feel right...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Don't worry, my guardian knight.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Okay, fine, but only tonight. Tomorrow's a big day, and many no-good scumbags are gonna take advantage of that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *yawn*

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Oh, you two must be exhausted from your long journey back to the city. My apologies for not realizing this sooner.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I've already prepared a room for you to rest. Please follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, you're so thoughtful! Paimon's so ready!

choices.text: Instead, we were only left with more questions...
It's a very important festival, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Here we are. It's also fairly close to where I've been staying.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks really nice!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry for the trouble, Dunyarzad.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hehe, not at all. Just tell me more about your adventures when you next get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's Paimon's specialty! Paimon can tell you stories next time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About our plans for tomorrow...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, if you don't mind, how about we all walk around together tomorrow?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: All of my friends will be working the festival, and Dehya is still insisting on her "covert" protection...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah? It'll be pretty hard to relax and enjoy the festival if Dehya's constantly hovering over you, right?

choices.text: I'll keep you company tomorrow.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Then let's meet at the nearby bazaar first thing tomorrow morning. Have a great night!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's a deal! Good night, Dunyarzad!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I may be too excited to fall asleep tonight. See you tomorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's starting to really look forward to the Sabzeruz Festival, too! Will there be lots of yummy food?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, no... Thinking about food is just gonna keep Paimon up all night. The earlier we sleep, the better. Let's go inside, Traveler.

choices.text: It'll be easier to get information with your help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Did we oversleep...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should go meet Dunyarzad right away.

talks.objective: Go to the appointed place and talk to Dunyarzad

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon! I've been waiting for you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good morning, Dunyarzad! We must've overslept a little bit, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Not at all. I arrived early.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Phew... Today is finally here! I must cherish every moment as if it were gold.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've worked so hard for this day. You gotta enjoy it to the fullest!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hehe, you know it! It's just that... as expected, I had some trouble falling asleep last night. I'm hoping my body won't be too much of an issue today.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Well, shall we? Let's start with the stalls over there.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Atten-tion! Young soldiers, are you here to join our ranks?

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Okay, one moment... Hmm... It's the Moon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to take a look too... Is it...? It looks more like a pie that Paimon bit into.

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Hmm... Generally speaking, the Moon signifies... It means... Wait a moment...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is he really looking it up in a book...

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, I remember now. It means illusions and lies.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Illusions and lies...? That sounds rather ominous...

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Yes, but this book says that if you trust your intuition and overcome your fears, the sun will surely rise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's not even trying to hide his book anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: ...Naturally, fate will only ever show you the beginning of a journey. It is up to you to forge your own ending. Hehe, thank you so much. I'll keep that in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, it's nothing. I'm just learning as I go, haha... ha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess that was still pretty interesting. Okay, on to the next stall.

talks.objective: Give the divination materials to Kimiya

dialogues.speaker: Children
dialogues.text: Farris! Farris!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Atten-tion! Soldiers, fall into formation if you want any Yalda Candies!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a weird guy with a weird hat.

dialogues.speaker: Children
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Dunyarzad!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Miss Dunyarzad, the children love you even more than Yalda Candies.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: In the few short days it took to prepare for the Sabzeruz Festival, the children have all grown very fond of you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Uh... Ah, hallowed Knight of Flowers, it is an honor that you know my name!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: A—Ah, ahem... Atten-tion! In the name of Farris, the Knight of Flowers, I commend you on your contributions to the glorious Sabzeruz Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Alright, little soldiers, take your Yalda Candies and don't forget your loyalty to Lesser Lord Kusanali. Dismissed!

dialogues.speaker: Children
dialogues.text: Yes, Knight Farris!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Just what is going on here...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hehe. Farris, the Knight of Flowers, is another Sabzeruz Festival icon, and one immensely popular with children. In the past, the actor portraying Farris would also sit on a flower carriage.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to Miss Dunyarzad's sponsorship that the children can make such wonderful memories today.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: As are we to you, Vihar.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Not at all! Oh, speaking of tradition, do you want some Yalda Candies? They're a festival staple, and I happen to have some boxes readied here. Take a look and pick whichever one you want.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whichever one... Don't these boxes all look the same?

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Haha, this is the fun part. Each box contains a random flavor — it's up to the luck of the draw. Flavors include Lavender Melon, Harra Fruit, Sunsettia...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, those all sound pretty good...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: ...And there's also Lizard Tail and Onikabuto.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? What's up with those two flavors?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Onikabuto is a little spicier than Lizard Tail.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad, y—you tried them before! Hmm... Traveler, help Paimon pick one. Paimon wants the Sunsettia flavor!

choices.text: I doubt I'll be able to get the exact flavor you want...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's alright, Paimon believes in you!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe, I also believe in your intuition.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Great! These boxes of candy are numbered one to five from left to right. Which one do you want?

choices.text: Number one.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number one.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Atten-tion! That's unfortunately Lizard Tail.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Paimon thought you survived so many epic battles because you had incredible luck, but looks like Paimon was wrong.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: The Sunsettia-flavored candy was in box number four. How about this? The most important thing is that everyone has a good time at the festival, so please take both boxes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!? Thanks a lot, Knight of Candies!

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: It's Knight of Flowers! Not Knight of Candies!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe... Paimon really wilted the carriage-less Knight of Flowers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They all basically sound the same! We got our candy, so let's keep going.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Oh, actually, I just remembered that I left something behind. Since you're here...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Can you come with me to get it?

choices.text: Not a problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad, you probably forgot because you're so excited about the Sabzeruz Festival!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Haha, how embarrassing.

choices.text: Sure thing.
Number two.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number two.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Atten-tion! That's unfortunately Harra Fruit.

choices.text: Number three.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number three.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Atten-tion! That's unfortunately Lavender Melon.

choices.text: Number four.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number four.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Haha, excellent work! That is indeed Sunsettia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon bet you survived so many epic battles because you had incredible luck, and Paimon was right!

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Atten-tion! Here's your Sunsettia-flavored candy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, thanks a lot, Knight of Candies!

choices.text: Number five.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely number five.

response.speaker: Vihar
response.text: Atten-tion! That's unfortunately Onikabuto.

choices.text: Don't blame me if I choose the wrong one.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad, are you okay? You look a little pale. Are you in shock?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I—I'm fine... My body always reacts like this whenever I exert myself too much...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure you're okay...?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Phew... I'll be fine after some rest. I'm more worried about Dehya... After all, none of this would've happened if I hadn't insisted on coming out today...

choices.text: Don't worry, she's tough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, don't worry!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Dunyarzad wait nearby for a while...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My lady, Traveler, found ya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dehya! You took care of 'em so fast.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Any more of them? Or rather, did anyone follow you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No, I just checked.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Dehya, your arm...!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Oh, this? I'm fine — it's just a scratch. Normally, they wouldn't have been able to land a hit on me at all, but I'm still getting used to this new greatsword.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Please let me take a closer look...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: C'mon, it's nothing. Us mercs aren't as fragile as you think.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hold on, you said something about a new greatsword? What happened to the one you were using before?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Uh... About that... Well... I sold it 'cause I was low on Mora. Stuff like this happens every now and then.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It can't be... The anonymous donation that was used for the venue's final round of preparations...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: *sigh* Hehe...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Uh, hey, Miss Dunyarzad, I wasn't trying to make you cry. I'm not gonna lose my commission because I made my employer cry, am I?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...Pfft... Hehe... Okay, making your employer cry won't affect your commission, but selling your weapon without permission and getting hurt... I'll have to re-evaluate your performance.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hahaha... You're so unreasonable, my lady.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hahaha...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...Thank you very much, Dehya.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ... *sigh* Don't be like that. I get embarrassed really easily.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: *cough* *cough*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you feeling unwell again, Dunyarzad?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: My lady, your condition... Traveler, can you take her somewhere to rest? I'll look around the area to make sure we're safe from an ambush.

choices.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Truly... I'm sorry for the trouble, everyone...

choices.text: Leave it to me.
She's protecting you because she agrees with you.

dialogues.speaker: Badis
dialogues.text: ...Tch, we're too late. Who knew the little lady was such an early riser.

dialogues.speaker: Idder
dialogues.text: I know, right... Hey, wait a minute. Boss, isn't that her?

dialogues.speaker: Badis
dialogues.text: Oh, that most certainly is! We're in luck. She's walking right into our clutches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those Eremites don't look like they're up to any good...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: ...Who are you? I don't believe the Homayanis hired you?

dialogues.speaker: Badis
dialogues.text: Heh, that's right. We haven't received any of their Mora, but... I wonder how much the Homayanis would shell out to get you back?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're a gang of kidnappers! Traveler, hurry and protect Dunyarzad!

choices.text: We'll be fine...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey! Did you scumbags even consider that the Homayanis might've hired a merc that outclasses you?

response.speaker: Badis
response.text: You're... Dehya!? Dehya the Flame-Mane... No wonder we mercs haven't heard anything about you for so long. You sold your unruly mane to the highest bidder.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Don't speak so disrespectfully. My family started working with her as gratitude for her past kindness to us...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Don't worry about it, my lady. Just some friendly banter between mercs. One punch and those rabid dogs will expose themselves for what they really are.

response.speaker: Badis
response.text: Hmph, aren't your claws all dull by now? Don't get too cocky!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Traveler, take Miss Dunyarzad to a safe location.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, we're gonna stay and help. There's too many of them!

choices.text: We can't guarantee anyone's safety here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm... You're right. Alright, fine!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Please be careful, Dehya.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Don't waste your time worrying about me — this is my job. Look out for yourself. After I've wiped the floor with them, I'll go find you all.

choices.text: Dehya's top priority is her employer's safety.
Professional here, ready to go.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: ...Were you not aware that the law prohibits this type of performance from taking place without prior permission?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there... Someone's yelling at Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I think I just saw the Akademiya's Grand Sage... Why is he here in person?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: But the Dance of Sabzeruz is one of the key parts of the Sabzeruz Festival. If we can't perform it...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: The Sabzeruz Festival... The law also prohibits the private hosting of large-scale, religious festivals. Only the Akademiya can host such an event.

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: If you continue to resist, we will have to order an investigation into every single event organizer...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage has already granted you much leniency. I advise that you exercise tact.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: How... How did things turn out like this...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: The Akademiya was originally responsible for the Sabzeruz Festival, but they've failed this responsibility for many years. I need to speak with them...

choices.text: Don't go. They have the final say in all of this.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...This is a hard pill to swallow, but... sigh, you're right. Things would only get worse.

response.speaker: Azar
response.text: Art... Dance... Aren't you ashamed of pursuing such frivolous and meaningless activities in this land of knowledge and reason?

response.speaker: Azar
response.text: Our Archon created the utopia that is Sumeru City for all scholars who sought validity, verity, and truth... while people like you wish to defile it.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: No, I believe that our Archon never rejected the arts. Even the Goddess of Flowers dedicated a dance to her...

response.speaker: Azar
response.text: With your lack of intellectual credentials, I do not believe you are qualified to debate with me. What you should be doing is finding workers to tear down this ridiculous eyesore.

response.speaker: Azar
response.text: When we return, have the Scribe draft an ordinance before the next Jnagarbha Day that prohibits public art performances. We will announce it to the public later via the Akasha.

response.speaker: Setaria
response.text: Understood. I will inform him when I return.

response.speaker: Azar
response.text: The Sabzeruz Festival... Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nilou, are you okay?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, Dunyarzad. You all saw that just now...? The Grand Sage ordered us to stop the performance...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Let's go somewhere the Akademiya can't find us and perform there... Ahh, but how do we let everyone know... And what about the atmosphere and the stage...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Or we could get people to block them off so they can't interrupt the performance... Agh... No, they just threatened to investigate the organizers. If we were caught...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Nilou, it's alright. Don't worry about it.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: But you've been looking forward to the Dance of Sabzeruz so much, and I know how important this festival is to you. I don't want you to have any regrets...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It's okay. Seeing you care this much about my feelings is more than enough.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It would be too risky to continue the Sabzeruz Festival at this point. I don't want to get everyone in trouble...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: ...If you say so, but... You can sneak out for the next Sabzeruz Festival, right? We'll make sure the next one is a smashing success!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: *sigh* The next one...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...Yes! Okay, it's a promise! It WILL be a smashing success!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't believe this is how things turned out. Those heartless geezers...

choices.text: Is there anything else we can do?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It really is okay. There's nothing we can do about it.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: *sigh* Still... I'd be lying if I said I had no regrets. I would have loved to see Nilou's dance.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The Sabzeruz Festival was forced to come to an unfortunately abrupt end...

choices.text: Should we try to think of another way?
If we force their hand too much, the situation may get ugly.

talks.objective: Take Dunyarzad somewhere nearby and rest
Take Dunyarzad somewhere nearby and rest

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: *pant* Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you feeling better, Dunyarzad?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Yes, much better. Just give me a few moments, and I'll be good to go.

choices.text: Dehya's expression just now, when she mentioned your condition...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...I didn't realize you were concerned about it. I guess I shouldn't continue to keep it a secret.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I was actually... born with Eleazar. It's terminal now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Eleazar!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can't believe it's Eleazar...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Oh? You've already heard of Eleazar. In that case, you probably know about its severity.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Sumeru's current medical advancements still haven't been able to find a cure. The disease's progression can only be delayed through environmental therapy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: There's no need to be sad. I've always lived with Eleazar, and I came to terms with it a long time ago.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Compared to the simple fact that I am afflicted with this, its effects on my life have been much more painful.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I know that my family loves me dearly. They've done all they can to provide the best environment for me, so that I can live for that much longer. However, I know... I will one day succumb to this.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Did you know? Before I ran away from home this time... the world outside of my home didn't even know that I existed.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Since I was a child, all I could do was sit on my bed and stare at everything outside of my window.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I'm sure my family is worried and disappointed in me for running away, but I... I just didn't wanna have any regrets.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I wanted to meet other people. To me, there is nothing more beautiful than being able to meet and speak with others.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Not to mention the incredible time spent preparing for the festival, the joy on everyone's faces here, and all the support I've received from friends like Dehya...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: This way, when my final day does arrive, it will be less sorrowful.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: At the very least, many people will remember that I once existed in this world, right?

choices.text: Yes. I will remember you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—As long as you don't forget Paimon, Paimon also won't forget about you! Ah... No, even if you forget Paimon, Paimon will still remember you!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe... Thank you two so much. I apologize for the depressing conversation. This is... This is out-of-character for me.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: To be honest, Lesser Lord Kusanali gave me the courage to do all of this. If it weren't for her encouragement, I wouldn't have taken that first step.

choices.text: You're the one who has remained resolute in the face of your illness.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...Thanks. There will always be frustrations in life, but I know that the point of living is not to leave behind any regrets.

choices.text: Right.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Oh, right! Isn't it almost time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Almost time for what?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Isn't the Dance of Sabzeruz about to begin? It's the part of the festival that I've been looking forward to the most...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Nilou will recreate that legendary scene with her most splendid dancing, and the Sabzeruz Festival will conclude amid everyone's applause and blessings...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: And with that, my wish will also...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then what are we waiting for? Let's go to the stage!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...Yeah! We should still make it in time!

choices.text: That's a wonderful mindset.
You're already so strong for never giving up.
Don't say that. You still have happy times yet to come.
Just how serious is your illness?

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Bazaar and see the Dance of Sabzeruz
Return to the accommodation and rest

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: So, how about it? Want to give it a try?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* A lot happened today... It's a shame the festival ended the way it did...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou and Dunyarzad promised to make the next Sabzeruz Festival a success... But Dunyarzad is running out of time...

choices.text: I'm sure she knows that very well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's getting late, and we got up really early today. Let's head back and rest...
*beep*

choices.text: This may be a regret that can never be resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: This is... a stall offering foods from the Haft-Mewa Feast.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: Oh-ho, you could tell straight away! I thought most people nowadays wouldn't know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mushrooms, flowers, and all kinds of fruit... It's all vegetarian stuff. Paimon's a little disappointed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what's the "Haft-Mewa Feast" you mentioned just now?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: It's another Sabzeruz Festival tradition. People used to set their tables with seven different foods...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Generally speaking, the most common selections were foods like Rukkhashava Mushrooms, Nilotpala Lotuses, Sumeru Roses, Sunsettias, Kalpalatas, Harra Fruits, and Zaytun Peaches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the Sabzeruz Festival is a vegetarian holiday...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hehe... You don't have to be a vegetarian to enjoy the spread. We just use the seven foods to symbolize the seven virtues of the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but if that's the case... If Sumeru uses vegetarian food to represent the Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then wouldn't the Pyro Archon's festival be full of food like roasted fowl, juicy meatballs, grilled steak...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler, we have to go to Natlan as soon as possible!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hahaha... I hope your wish comes true one day, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks! Alright, how about we also check out some of these other stalls?

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Dear customers, would you like to try your hand at alchemical divination?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's alchemical divination? Those two things sound like they'd be fun to try together.

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: Right? I thought the same when I first heard about it. It is said to be a mysterious craft invented by none other than Lesser Lord Kusanali herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... how does it work?

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: It's quite simple. After you give me any two alchemical reagents, I'll use them to perform a random transmutation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure sounds random... So random that it'll probably fail.

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: That is precisely what we need. After the transmutation fails, your one and only diviner here will interpret the remnants.

choices.text: For some reason... I don't buy it.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Well... According to Lesser Lord Kusanali, everything is interconnected, and all that occurs can be traced back to fate. You can say this is a pearl of old wisdom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why does everything sound so much more credible when Dunyarzad says it? Are you guys working together?

response.speaker: Kimiya
response.text: So that's the true wisdom behind it! This young lady sure knows her stuff. So, how about it? Want to give it a try?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, I guess I can give it a go.

choices.text: This entire thing is way too random.

dialogues.speaker: Amal
dialogues.text: I picked all of these from the forest yesterday, so their freshness is guaranteed!

dialogues.speaker: Kimiya
dialogues.text: The diviner's interpretation is the most important part of alchemical divination. I just consulted the book to make sure you got the correct message.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't miss the Sabzeruz Festival, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's hurry and find Dunyarzad. Paimon thinks... she must be around the Grand Bazaar, since she showed us around there last time.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Many vendors came out of the blue to support the event, and they insisted on covering costs themselves. Let's go give them some business.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They paid for everything out-of-pocket? Sounds like they're not in this just for the Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hehe, they all said that contributing to a lively festival atmosphere is more important than money, especially since we don't often get to celebrate Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, they're selling food over that way! Let's go take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: They say the Sabzeruz Festival was very lively a long, long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Large flower carriages used to parade through the city. As they headed towards Port Ormos, people would throw flowers, candy, and liquor all along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad's eyes are sparkling right now!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wish I could have seen that spectacle. But if you ask me, I'm sure Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz will be just as impressive!
